newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk praises Cambodian PM for talking peace.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk praises Cambodian PM for talking peace.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk praised co-Premier Hun Sen on Saturday for calling a detente in the troubled coalition government's recent war of words and put strong pressure on his son to follow suit.

"I thank and congratulate very warmly Samdech Hun Sen for his aforementioned declarations which cannot bring to everyone (anything) but relief, joy and gratitude," Sihanouk said in a written interview with the staff of his monthly bulletin that was released on Saturday.

Sihanouk said he hoped his son, co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, "will soon make a declaration of a total and irreversible suspension of the 'war of words' and other forms (violent or otherwise) of confrontation."

The troubled relationship between Hun Sen and Ranariddh, former battlefield foes who share power in an uneasy coalition government formed after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, reached new lows in recent weeks.

Bitter feuds over power sharing, the role of royalists in politics and a March 30 grenade attack on opposition leader and Ranariddh ally Sam Rainsy have fuelled the two leaders' dislike for each other and spurred a heated war of words.
But last week, Hun Sen called for detente, pledging to stop his angry rhetoric and vowing to revoke his previous opposition to royalist participation in politics.
In the monthly bulletin, Sihanouk embraced what his interviewers called Hun Sen's "new look".

But he did not comment on their suggestions that Hun Sen was motivated by foreign pressure, the failure of a royalist party split to gain broad support or Sihanouk's promises not to enter politics and challenge Hun Sen.
Sihanouk instead reasserted his pledge to remain above politics until his death, while sounding a defiant note with a vow to remain on the throne despite anti-royalist opposition.
"I am and I will remain the king of everyone, including Khmer (Cambodian) republicans who hate me, reject me and want to sink the monarchy," he concluded.
The next elections are expected in the country before the end of 1998.
